quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO Dado Alonso): group revenue of $228,000,000, up 547% year over year and 56% from Q3; annualized run-rate revenue for the core business of $1,200,000,000 at December, above the high end of the Q3 guidance range of $1,100,000,000. The core AI cloud business grew revenue 830% year over year and 63% quarter over quarter, 'driven by high utilization, strong pricing, and strong execution'; its adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 19% in Q3 to 24%. Group adjusted EBITDA inflected positively in Q4, at a 7% margin. Year-end cash and cash equivalents of $3,000,000,000; Q4 operating cash flow of $834,000,000, 'primarily comprised of upfront payments from our long-term agreements'. Revenue came in the middle of guidance while ARR beat it; management called ARR 'the north star metric' in the hypergrowth phase.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $228,000,000 (547% YoY); ARR $1,200,000,000; AI cloud adj. EBITDA margin 24%; group adj. EBITDA margin 7%; operating cash flow $834,000,000

quarterly_data.signal: Initial FY2026 guidance: annualized run-rate revenue of between $7,000,000,000 and $9,000,000,000 by 2026 reiterated, and full-year revenue of between $3,000,000,000 and $3,400,000,000. The gap between ARR and revenue reflects the deployment schedule, with 'the majority of this capacity being installed in the second half of the year', and the largest enterprise partnerships still ramping; new sites start coming online from Q2. Group adjusted EBITDA margin expected at approximately 40% for 2026 (other businesses still at an EBITDA loss); EBIT to remain at a loss in 2026 while GPUs deploy and R&D grows; medium-term EBIT target of 20% to 30% maintained. Management: 'Our 2026 ARR target is not dependent on any new mega deals'; hyperscaler-size deals stay opportunistic. Starting in Q1 2026 the depreciation schedule moves from four years to five years 'to reflect what we are seeing in the market and in our current utilization commitments'.
quarterly_data.figure: ARR between $7,000,000,000 and $9,000,000,000; revenue between $3,000,000,000 and $3,400,000,000; group adj. EBITDA margin approximately 40%; medium-term EBIT 20% to 30%; depreciation four years to five years

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 CAPEX PLAN (initial): $16,000,000,000 to $20,000,000,000, with about 60% of the capital needed already in hand from the balance sheet, existing operations and commitments; cash flows (cash on hand, cash from the core business and, 'most importantly', upfront cash from the favorable terms of long-term agreements) will finance 'the majority, actually around 60%, maybe even more' of 2026 CapEx needs. Split of the vertically integrated CapEx: less than 10% to secure power, approximately 20% to build data centers, the remainder to deploy GPUs, which are deployed in a short time period when there is 'great visibility about the demand and about the prices and about our margins'. Nebius had no corporate-level debt and no asset-backed financing ('we did not have it to date by choice'); it is exploring adding corporate debt and asset-backed financing and plans during 2026 to move toward 'a more optimal capital structure'; the ATM equity program launched last November was unused, with no concrete near-term plans to use it. Stakes in ClickHouse (over a 25% stake) and other businesses are named as future capital sources. Management said the CapEx sizing rests on 'clear visibility on the demand for 2026 and for 2027, both from our cloud clients as well as from AI labs and hyperscalers' and lays the foundation for 'hypergrowth 2027 and beyond'.
quarterly_data.figure: CapEx $16,000,000,000 to $20,000,000,000; about 60% of the capital needed in hand; power less than 10%, data centers approximately 20%

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY: nine new data centers across the globe announced on the call day ('nine contracted sites'). Contracted power was already more than 2 gigawatts in February versus the prior goal of 2.5 gigawatts by the end of the year, so the 2026 forecast was raised to more than 3 gigawatts; 800 megawatts to 1 gigawatt of that is on track to be available data center capacity around year-end. Colocations drive growth starting in Q2 2026 and ramp through the year, some bigger projects come online at the end of 2026, and Nebius' own projects 'will really start to ramp up in 2027 and beyond'. Preference is to self-develop the largest projects (better total cost of ownership, execution control, design tailored to its technical requirements), using leases and partnerships to fill gaps until own builds are at full speed.
quarterly_data.figure: contracted power more than 2 gigawatts; 2026 forecast more than 3 gigawatts (prior 2.5 gigawatts); 800 megawatts to 1 gigawatt available capacity

quarterly_data.signal: DEMAND AND PRICING: sold out of capacity in Q3 and Q4 2025 and 'already now in 2026 also sold out' ('Even before we bring capacity online, it is often sold out.'). Average contract duration of new cloud customers grew by 50%, and GPU prices 'did not fall even on previous generations of GPUs, as the industry may have expected'. Marc Boroditsky: 'very strong pricing across all families of GPUs' at full utilization; in Q4 nearly twice as many transactions over 12 months in duration as in Q3, while average selling prices increased by more than 50%; 'we are sold out of Hoppers', and Hopper capacity coming up for renewal, often off short reserve agreements, is renewing at 12 months or longer with 'pricing nudging up'. Q1 2026 pipeline creation on track to exceed $4,000,000,000; more customers willing to prepay to secure future capacity. AI-native customers that used to order hundreds or thousands of GPUs 'are ordering tens of thousands of GPUs', while 'access to compute remains constrained'.
quarterly_data.figure: average contract duration grew by 50%; average selling prices increased by more than 50%; Q1 pipeline creation to exceed $4,000,000,000

quarterly_data.signal: SUPPLY CHAIN: on data center equipment shortages, management said a portfolio of sites plus full-stack flexibility (moving loads between locations) keeps guidance from depending on any single project, and it has already contracted the majority of long-lead items for its own sites to secure deployment beyond 2026. On the memory and storage shortage: for its largest deals, with Microsoft and Meta, Nebius was 'able to secure the necessary components last year for the full scope of those contracts' and 'secured it in 2025, before any price increase'; it is confident its supply chain will deliver the parts for the remaining capacity. At the New Jersey site, 'our partners secured the components in the supply chain', and project plans carry safety-margin buffer time.

PLATFORM: first M&A deal, the acquisition of Tavily, an agentic search company that connects AI agents to the web, already serves many Fortune 500 customers and brings almost 700,000 developers to the platform; more acquisitions are possible. Recently launched Token Factory (Nebius is exploring consumption-based per-token pricing) and Aether releases, which open enterprise TAM. All AI cloud customers use Nebius' AI cloud software, 'a 100% attach rate', which lets it 'charge more on a relative per GPU-hour'. Continued demand for embedded storage in physical AI, media and entertainment, and healthcare and life sciences; go-to-market leans into the healthcare and life sciences, media and entertainment, physical AI and retail verticals.

contracts.signal: Meta contract fully delivered: 'As of early February, Meta’s capacity was fully deployed and we are now fully servicing their contract.' Both contracted tranches were delivered on time early in February 2026 and went live then; Nebius expects to recognize 12 months of revenue for the first tranche and roughly 11 months for the second tranche. Components for the full scope of the contract were secured in 2025, before any price increase.

Microsoft delivery schedule (discussed under the New Jersey data center update): the first tranche was delivered on time in November; the remaining tranches deliver throughout 2026, with more than half landing in the second half of the year. Microsoft revenue ramps with the tranches in 2026 and Microsoft 'will begin to deliver a full-year revenue starting in 2027', at the full annual run rate once all tranches are deployed. Components for the full scope of the contract were secured in 2025, before any price increase.
contracts.units: first tranche delivered; remaining tranches throughout 2026
